idiom_name: final case class Effectivity(from: LocalDate, until: Option[LocalDate]) + Ordering[LocalDate]
implementation_notes: Scala gets java.time through the JVM but not the ergonomics: java.time.LocalDate implements Comparable[ChronoLocalDate] rather than Comparable[LocalDate], so Scala's Ordering/Ordered instances are not derived and `from < until` does not compile without an instance - define one (implicit val dateOrdering: Ordering[LocalDate] = Ordering.by(_.toEpochDay), or the Scala 3 `given` form) and keep it in a single domain package object. With that instance a case class holding from and Option[LocalDate] until, plus contains/overlaps methods, is the whole pattern: case classes give value semantics through equals/hashCode/copy, and pattern matching on Option makes the open end explicit. The library variant (ThreeTen-Extra LocalDateRange) is preferable when overlap/abut semantics must be interoperable with Java services.
pitfalls: Without an explicit Ordering[LocalDate] the natural comparisons do not compile (LocalDate is Comparable[ChronoLocalDate]); defining the instance in two places makes the two orderings drift.
Option[LocalDate] is total but noisy: scattering .forall/.exists over domain code hides whether an open end is allowed - model that decision once (or use an explicit OpenEnded/Closed ADT).

java.time is a JVM platform type: Scala.js and Scala Native have no java.time implementation, so a JVM-targeted domain type silently makes the module non-multiplatform (scala-java-time provides the same API on JS, but nothing on Native).

variants.name: ThreeTen-Extra LocalDateRange from Scala
variants.implementation_notes: The Java range type is usable directly from Scala: LocalDateRange stores the start inclusive and the end exclusive and offers contains, overlaps, abuts, isConnected, intersection, union and span, so the pattern degenerates to a case class holding one range plus an as-of predicate, and the half-open convention is fixed by the library instead of by convention. Interoperability with Java services and a tested overlap algebra are the reasons to prefer it; choose the case-class variant when the period must carry domain behaviour (a precedence rule between intentionally overlapping assignments, retroactive corrections) that the library range does not express.
pitfalls: of() and ofClosed() differ by one day on identical inputs; adopting both in one codebase makes overlapping validations disagree.
LocalDateRange is a JVM library type: it cannot be used from Scala.js or Scala Native (scala-java-time does not ship ThreeTen-Extra).

The range is immutable, so the ordinary Scala idiom of copy()/with... does not exist on it - replacing a period means constructing a new LocalDateRange, and forgetting that yields code that appears to update nothing.
